status: Independent proposal saved before reading A or C; analytical synthetic example only; round 1 clarifications logged in debate/B_round1.md
recommended_core: Finite normalized distributions over coded answers to prespecified questions under an explicit acquisition/coding protocol; exact enumeration replaces corpus generation and Monte Carlo.

findings.claim: Replicate coded answers rather than text or whole historical worlds.
findings.scope: Only properties represented by the questions and acquisition protocol are checked.

findings.claim: Uncertain internal parameters are not necessary for predictive checking; a degenerate parameter distribution still permits replicated data.
findings.implication: Reframe mechanism decomposition as operational help and diagnostic structure, not a mathematical enabling condition.

findings.claim: Likelihood ratios alone do not determine absolute predictive probabilities.
findings.implication: Additional absolute probabilities or meaningful bounds are indispensable.

findings.claim: Distinguish same-data PPC, held-out posterior prediction, Bayes-factor updating, absolute inadequacy, and localized diagnosis.
findings.implication: A Bayes factor favoring a composite does not establish likelihood misspecification.

findings.claim: Treat complete configuration C as the latent state within model M, not a fixed configuration with separately uncertain component states.
Absence of recovered records requires a detection/false-positive model or conditional target with explicit limits.
Reserve source blocks and model joint or sequential conditional distributions; source separation alone does not guarantee statistical independence.
findings.implication: Do not count copied accounts or related statements as independent holdouts.

findings.claim: Use coherent sets of full probability models when elicitation is weak, propagate whole models, and report predictive envelopes.
findings.limitation: Wide sets may correctly yield no informative diagnosis; LLM agreement does not identify calibration.

findings.claim: A strongly discriminating result can be unsurprising absolutely.
findings.empirical_status: Synthetic limiting case with perfect recording, recovery and coding; no Chile validation
round1_clarifications: Complete archive does not imply perfect recording.
Small point probability alone does not establish inadequacy; T is a narrow prespecified directional check and a family of checks requires evaluation of the full alarm rule.

findings.claim: A few heterogeneous checks cannot establish calibration or uniquely localize a faulty causal link.
findings.implication: Report tension and candidate components; require further independent observations for adjudication.

debate_positions.against_full_corpus_requirement: Need only the marginal observation distribution for targets, but must defend acquisition and coding assumptions.
debate_positions.against_verbal_only_PPC: Ordinal plausibility is useful but cannot identify absolute model inadequacy and should not be labeled PPC.
debate_positions.publication_contribution: Operational protocol plus minimal-information and insufficiency results, with prospective blocked evaluation; not novelty of Bayesian integration.

primary_sources_added.title: Gneiting and Raftery 2007, Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
primary_sources_added.used_for: Proper scores evaluate probabilistic predictions in expectation, not proof of calibration from one result.

primary_sources_added.title: Dawid 1984, Statistical Theory: The Prequential Approach
Stan User's Guide, Posterior and Prior Predictive Checks
primary_sources_added.used_for: Observed and replicated data compared through same statistic.
